back:
1. Check that the code follows the rules of C++. If not, it reports an error (with a line number) and aborts.
2. Translate the C++ into machine-language instructions.

Those instructions are stored in an object file, typically name.o or name.obj, matching the .cpp file it came from. One .cpp file produces one object file.
front: What two jobs does a C++ compiler perform? What is an object file?
